neighbours.label: Other people's feelings as the reaction to someone's conduct or fame: the subject/verb of the reacting crowd ('⟦People⟧ know who you are', 'they will ⟦feel⟧ obligated', 'makes a lot of ⟦people⟧ laugh'). The - pole holds the attitude verb itself (hated, love, dislike).
fire: If you listen patiently to your staff, they will feel respected and work harder.
When a host remembers your name, guests feel flattered and tend to return.
Speak honestly to an audience and they will feel that you trust them.
If you thank volunteers in public, they will feel proud of what they did.
Treat the new pupils warmly and they will feel at home within a week.
When a shop refunds without arguing, customers feel grateful and tell their friends.
Give the players a say in training and they will feel responsible for the result.
If you apologise quickly to neighbours, they will feel far less resentful.
quiet: If you oil the hinges regularly, the gate will swing quietly and last longer.
When a kettle reaches the boil, the switch clicks off and the light goes out.
Store the apples in a cool cellar and they will keep until early spring.
If you prune roses in winter, they will flower more heavily in June.
Leave the dough near the stove and it will double in size within an hour.
When a river floods in spring, the fields stay wet and planting is delayed.
Give the engine fresh oil and it will run for another ten thousand miles.
If you salt the path tonight, the ice will melt by morning.

notes: Card: ' they' x6, ' People', ' feel', ' buy'. Probe was weak: 'they will feel welcome' 0.46, 'People recognise her' 0.17, 'a lot of people forget' 0.16; non-human consequences 0.04. Label is a guess at the shared pattern; a fail would be informative.
